rounds.text: Gravity (India) Ltd is dramatically under-appreciated by the market, trading at an exceptionally low P/E of 4.55x [E1] compared to a sector benchmark of 15.09x [E6], alongside a modest EV/EBITDA of 3.48x [E8] relative to its peers at 8.89x [E11]. The underlying fundamental performance is staggering, highlighted by trailing twelve month sales growth of 1316% [E17], profit growth of 1512% [E21], and an astronomical TTM return on equity of 151% [E29] that crushes the sector benchmark of 6.88% [E9]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow analysis estimates intrinsic value at Rs 131 per share against a current market price of just Rs 14.6 [E42], leaving a massive margin of safety of 88.8% [E43]. The company is nearly debt-free with a pristine debt-to-equity ratio of 0.07x [E37], [E49] and a 4-year trend of increasing operating margins [E32] that currently sit at a robust 11% [E30]. Conceded: promoter holding has dropped to 6.05% [E40] and cash conversion for Mar 2026 stood at 0.00x [E34]. Nevertheless, profit growth is vastly outpacing the modest 30% five-year share price growth [E23], [E45], signaling a major turnaround where market sentiment has critically lagged behind actual business performance [E61].

Despite headline figures showing recent profitability, serious structural risks undermine the stability of Gravity (India) Ltd. Most concerningly, the cash conversion ratio sits at 0.00x for March 2026, with operating cash flow and free cash flow both stagnating at Rs 0 Cr, meaning reported profits are completely divorced from actual cash generation and point toward heavy receivables or accruals [E34, E35, E36]. Compounding this alarming disconnect between paper earnings and cash, insiders are fleeing the stock; promoter holding has collapsed by 18.16 percentage points since December 2023 down to a negligible 6.05% as of September 2026 [E40]. Furthermore, the longer-term historical track record reveals a chronically weak business, evidenced by a 10-year median return on equity of just 1% and a 5-year median ROE of only 9% [E26, E27]. The screening mechanism itself flags that earnings growth is actively decelerating [E60], while the quarterly operating margin trend reads inconsistent over the last two quarters [E33]. Conceded: [E14], [E18], [E21], [E42].

Conceded: [E34], [E35], [E36], [E40]. While the bear highlights these cash flow and promoter holding figures, the company's operational execution tells a powerfully improving story through soaring metrics, including a 5-year compounded profit growth of 115% and a trailing twelve month profit growth of 1512% [E19, E21]. The bear's citation of historical median ROE overlooks the explosive recent reality where 3-year median ROE reaches 25% and the latest annual ROE hits 151% [E28, E29]. Operating margins have turned around dramatically, expanding by 361 percentage points over three years to reach 11% in the TTM period [E30]. Furthermore, the business is practically debt-free with a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.07x and reduced debt overall [E37, E48, E49]. Dismissing this fundamental turnaround based on stale historical averages or temporary sentiment misses how drastically the company's earning power has outpaced its share price [E45, E46, E61].

Conceded: [E19, E21, E28, E29, E30]. While those soaring metrics are present in the filings, the bull ignores the stark absence of underlying cash generation, as operating and free cash flows sit at exactly Rs 0 Cr for Mar 2026, resulting in a zero cash conversion ratio that demands caution regarding reported profits [E34, E35, E36]. Furthermore, the bull minimizes the severe erosion of insider alignment, where promoter holding collapsed from 24.21% in Dec 2023 to just 6.05% by Sep 2026—a steep 18.16 percentage point drop that leaves insiders with skin barely in the game [E40, E53, E54]. The screen itself flags that earnings growth is actively decelerating, and the multi-year history shows a sluggish 1% median ROE over 10 years, proving that recent explosive figures rest on a volatile and historically weak foundation [E26, E60].
